Confederation of African Football Reverts to Biennial Afcon Schedule

01 Nov 2026, 10:43 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

2 min read

Key takeawaysThe Confederation of African Football (Caf) has confirmed that the Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle. This decision marks a significant reversal from the governing body's December announcement, which had signaled a transition toward a four-year tournament format.

Reversing the Four-Year Shift

The Confederation of African Football (Caf) has confirmed that the Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle. This decision marks a significant reversal from the governing body's December announcement, which had signaled a transition toward a four-year tournament format.

Caf President Patrice Motsepe stated that the return to the biennial schedule is intended to "advance, protect and promote the interests of African football" and its member associations, as well as the players active in international leagues. The move follows an internal review of the organization’s long-term financial and logistical planning.

Financial and Logistical Considerations

Caf had originally explored the implementation of an African Nations League as a replacement for the biennial Afcon. However, the governing body acknowledged that the proposed league would require several years to reach the level of self-sufficiency needed to replace the revenue generated by the established tournament.

Practical challenges associated with the biennial format include:

  • Scheduling Conflicts: Frequent overlaps with the European club football season.
  • Global Calendar Pressure: Constraints imposed by other international fixtures, such as Fifa’s expanded 32-team Club World Cup, which necessitated mid-season scheduling for previous iterations of the Afcon.

Future Hosting Roadmap

Following the reversal, Caf has outlined the tournament calendar for the coming years, noting a specific exception for the 2030 cycle due to the World Cup:

  • 2027: Jointly hosted by Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.
  • 2028: Tournament scheduled.
  • 2030: No tournament held, citing the World Cup schedule.
  • 2031 & 2033: Tournaments scheduled.

How to Verify Updates

For official information regarding tournament schedules, host nations, and administrative changes, interested parties should monitor the official Confederation of African Football (Caf) website and their verified media channels. Supporters can also follow statements released by individual national football associations for local impacts regarding player call-ups and tournament preparation.
